claims.statement: Recovering from a misclick is very poor; browser Back wipes the session and forces re-analysis.
Going back must be easy and never lose the analyzed repo.
Two hierarchies (treemap location vs dependency focus) and too many forms of navigation; closing the graph loses your place.
Treemap and dependency graph are a toggle on the same view, projections of one location and color overlay.
A history of places visited that can be opened to jump back.
Navigation state persisting across graph close/reopen is good; keep it.
Quick navigation from a node to its containing folder.
Animated canvas transition between treemap and dependency graph.
Navigation changes must not slow toggling or drilling.
Repo path, treemap root, metric, and filters are not in the URL; refresh lands on the empty state.
Toolbar Dependencies toggle doesn't clear depFocus; refresh reopens the graph.
No middle-click handler exists; graph 'open' is Ctrl/Cmd-click or double-click.
Treemap zoom and dependency focus are one location: drilling either moves both; one breadcrumb; the toggle only changes projection.
The dependency graph is fetched for the treemap current folder, so edges from outside that folder are missing; with one location it should be fetched for the repo root.

shape.appetite: Medium, client-only: a location module wired into treemap, graph, header, and compare entry/exit.
shape.problem: Several navigation mechanisms disagree; Back drops the repo; two breadcrumbs; no history; graph scoped to treemap folder hides outside dependents.

recommended_shape.history: pushState per location change + in-memory History dropdown (~30)

success_moves: URL as the single source of truth with real pushState entries; app signals derive from it
Fetch the dependency graph once for the repo root (server-cached) and focus within it: fixes missing outside dependents and keeps drills local
Keep the scan in a store that survives compare/normal switches so popstate never remounts or rescans
Pure location module (parse/serialize/push/history) covered by vitest before wiring
Visible node actions (Focus/Open code/Show folder) so navigation never depends on modifier clicks

first_proof.question: Can one URL-backed location with pushState make misclick recovery and refresh lossless without slowing navigation?
first_proof.artifact: location module + vitest, wired to treemap zoom and graph focus on srcly itself; in-app browser script
first_proof.observation: Back after misclick returns to prior focus with no scan request; refresh restores repo, at, and view; History dropdown lists visits
first_proof.decision_rule: pass -> toggle swap, node actions, compare no-remount, root-scoped graph fetch; refresh restore >~2s on modeler -> show cached last location while rescan validates

rabbit_holes: whole-repo graph first-open cost on large repos
treemap zoom to a symbol (scope highlight) semantics
